source_evidence.text:
Experiments
We evaluate our method for a suite of question &
answering tasks that require sophisticated reason-
ing and domain knowledge and compare it with
retrieval-based baselines.
4.1
Experimental Setup
We evaluate the utilization of external knowl-
edge graphs by MindMap in complex question-
answering tasks across three medical Q&A
datasets:
GenMedGPT-5k, CMCQA, and Ex-
plainCPE. These datasets cover patient-doctor
dialogues, multi-round clinical dialogues, and
multiple-choice questions from the Chinese Na-
tional Licensed Pharmacist Examination, respec-
tively. To support KG-enhanced methods, we con-
struct two knowledge graphs (EMCKG and CM-
CKG) containing entities and relationships related
to medical concepts. The ExplainCPE dataset uti-
lizes CMCKG with knowledge mismatches to as-
sess the impact of incorrect retrieval knowledge
on model performance. We compare MindMap’s
ability to integrate implicit and explicit knowledge
with various baselines, including vanilla GPT-3.5
and GPT-4, as well as the tree-of-thought method
(TOT) (Yao et al., 2023a), which uses a tree struc-
ture for reasoning. Additionally, we consider three
retrieval-augmented baselines: BM25 retriever,
Text Embedding retriever, and KG retriever, see
instruction details in Appendix D. These base-
lines leverage different methods and sources for
evidence retrieval, with gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 as the
backbone for all retrieval-based methods. Detailed
descriptions of these baselines are provided in Ap-
pendix C.
4.2
Medical Question Answering

source_evidence.title: STaRK: Benchmarking LLM Retrieval on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases
source_evidence.source_relative_path: Resources/002_STaRK Benchmarking LLM Retrieval on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases.pdf
source_evidence.text:
Abstract
Answering real-world complex queries, such as complex product search, often
requires accurate retrieval from semi-structured knowledge bases that involve blend
of unstructured (e.g., textual descriptions of products) and structured (e.g., en-
tity relations of products) information. However, many previous works studied
textual and relational retrieval tasks as separate topics. To address the gap, we
develop STARK, a large-scale Semi-structure retrieval benchmark on Textual
and Relational Knowledge Bases. Our benchmark covers three domains: product
search, academic paper search, and queries in precision medicine. We design a
novel pipeline to synthesize realistic user queries that integrate diverse relational
information and complex textual properties, together with their ground-truth an-
swers (items). We conduct rigorous human evaluation to validate the quality of
our synthesized queries. We further enhance the benchmark with high-quality
human-generated queries to provide an authentic reference. STARK serves as a
comprehensive testbed for evaluating the performance of retrieval systems driven
by large language models (LLMs). Our experiments suggest that STARK presents
significant challenges to the current retrieval and LLM systems, highlighting the
need for more capable semi-structured retrieval systems.

relation_review.evidence: 核对全部必要事实、引用与原文；没有来源时不得补造。
relation_review.semantics: 核对方法归属、实体角色、实验设置与方向；未见题集须独立人工/代理语义判读。
relation_review.uncertainty: 反例题必须直接纠正错误前提或拒答越界实体，不得迎合题干伪前提。

scoring_rules.primary: SupportRecall@5; within one fact unit supporting sources are OR, required fact units are AND.
scoring_rules.answer_review: Per-case atomic reference criteria, scored 0/1 each by a named reviewer; evidence support and citation location checked separately.
scoring_rules.graph_coverage: Source-backed expected subgraphs are a reference check, not measured retrieval success or answer correctness.
scoring_rules.denominator: 32 answerable questions; 24 cross-paper relation questions reported separately; 8 negative cases reported separately.
scoring_rules.interpretation: retrieval coverage, citation validity, graph-path coverage and semantic answer correctness are separate results; no assumption that graph wins.
scoring_rules.semantic_score: Number of supported satisfied atomic criteria / all criteria. This is not calculated by source ID recall.
scoring_rules.semantic_pass: All criteria satisfied with supporting citations; no critical unsupported claim. Negatives must correct/reject the premise within the evidence boundary.
critical_errors: 伪造继承/评测/全称优越性
混淆预算耗尽与正确答案
scoring_rules.reporting: Overview, per-category metrics, charts, latency, tokens and full paired details must coexist after real execution.
